9	# TaxKit repository guide
10	
11	TaxKit is the public monorepo for the open-source tax engine, API, SDK, and
12	documentation site. Start with [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md), the sole
13	maintainer-document lifecycle and truth-layer router. `CLAUDE.md` points to this
14	file; edit `AGENTS.md` only.
15	
16	## Operating loop
17	
18	1. Read `docs/README.md`, then only the semantic owner for the task.
19	2. Confirm the claim against code, configuration, Schemas, exports, generated
20	   owners, or external readback at the boundary it describes.
21	3. Put current implementation intent in a SPEC/task and active execution plan;
22	   never reopen completed work as policy.
23	4. Update the earliest durable owner and required pointers in the same slice.
24	5. Run `bun run check:docs`, `bun run check:runbooks` when operations changed,
25	   focused checks, and `bun run verification`;
26	   package-facing changes also need an appropriate Changeset.
27	6. Retain artifact identity, authority, postconditions, limitations,
28	   non-claims, and rollback.
29	
30	For any material calculator/rule/schema, SDK/export/example, HTTP/OpenAPI,
31	public MDX/navigation/runtime, package/app, command/CI/versioning/release-proof,
32	lifecycle, SPEC, plan, runbook, or skill change, invoke the repository-local
33	`$docs-maintainer` route before accepting the slice. Record `Change required`,
34	`Preserve`, or evidenced `N/A` for its documentation impact. Scheduled or
35	background freshness work is report-only candidate output unless a separately
36	attached implementation authority names the reviewer and publisher.
37	
38	## Task routes
39	
40	- Repository and package topology:
41	  [`docs/architecture/README.md`](docs/architecture/README.md), then
42	  [`docs/architecture/package-ownership.md`](docs/architecture/package-ownership.md).
43	- Effect services and boundaries:
44	  [`docs/architecture/effect-services.md`](docs/architecture/effect-services.md)
45	  and the applicable package README.
46	- API/SDK: [`docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md`](docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md),
47	  [`apps/api/README.md`](apps/api/README.md), and
48	  [`packages/sdk/typescript/README.md`](packages/sdk/typescript/README.md).
49	- Calculators/rules/facts: the focused owner under `docs/architecture/` and the
50	  owning package README.
51	- Frontend/public docs:
52	  [`docs/architecture/frontend.md`](docs/architecture/frontend.md),
53	  [`docs/architecture/content-and-posts.md`](docs/architecture/content-and-posts.md),
54	  and [`apps/docs/README.md`](apps/docs/README.md).
55	- Current work: [`docs/product-specs/index.md`](docs/product-specs/index.md) and
56	  [`docs/exec-plans/active/README.md`](docs/exec-plans/active/README.md).
57	- Standards, tests, and release checks:
58	  [`docs/standards/README.md`](docs/standards/README.md) and
59	  [`docs/architecture/testing-and-quality.md`](docs/architecture/testing-and-quality.md).
60	- Repeatable release, versioning, packed-consumer and recovery operations:
61	  [`docs/runbooks/README.md`](docs/runbooks/README.md) and
62	  [`docs/operations/authority-model.md`](docs/operations/authority-model.md).
63	- References and audits: [`docs/references/README.md`](docs/references/README.md)
64	  and [`docs/documentation-audit/README.md`](docs/documentation-audit/README.md).
65	
66	## Engineering guardrails
67	
68	- Use Effect-native Schema, branded identities, Config, services, Layers,
69	  tagged errors, collections, Command, and runtime primitives when they own the
70	  semantics. Decode unknown/representation ingress once and encode egress at
71	  explicit boundaries.
72	- Reuse owning Schemas and schema-derived types. Do not mirror raw `id: string`,
73	  DTOs, provider types, primitive semantic config, or unchecked SDK output.
74	- Keep primary Effects flat, sequential, and pipe-first where that clarifies
75	  data flow. Keep one-use mapping/decoding/error logic inline; reject
76	  helper/common/utils sprawl and generic SDK callback wrappers.
77	- Keep service contracts, live Layers, test Layers, and executable composition
78	  separate. Do not run Effects or build live Layers inside domain logic.
79	- Provider clients expose named Effect operations, `Config.schema` with
80	  redacted secrets, immediate Schema decoding, safe tagged errors without
81	  `instanceof`, and live/mock Layers.
82	- React composition flows route → policy-owning container → focused leaf.
83	  Routes own transport restoration/outcome matching, containers own commands
84	  and coordination, and leaves render readonly values/local interaction state.
85	- Admit an abstraction only with semantic weight, an owner, a real reuse or
86	  substitution point, a simpler call graph, and focused proof.
87	
88	## Authority and proof
89	
90	Tool access is capability, not authority. Provider, registry, publication,
91	release, deployment, credential, and destructive operations require a named
92	principal, operation, resource, environment, approval boundary, receipt,
93	rollback/revocation, and readback. Local gates do not prove publication,
94	production, or external consumer behavior.
95	
96	Use `bun run check:repository-paths` for checkout portability and
97	`bun run verification` for repository closeout. Use `bun run release:check`
98	only for its documented local release-evidence graph; it does not authorize or
99	prove publication.
100

10	# TaxKit documentation
11	
12	This is the sole router for maintainer-document type, lifecycle, truth layers,
13	and semantic ownership. Root `README.md` is the public repository entry point;
14	`AGENTS.md` is the short task map; `docs/architecture/README.md` is the current
15	architecture route. Public documentation content is a separate product surface
16	owned by `apps/docs` and the docs packages.
17	
18	## Truth layers
19	
20	Use the strongest applicable owner and link rather than copy:
21	
22	1. External systems own their current external state at readback time.
23	2. Code, configuration, Schemas, package exports, workflows, and generated
24	   sources own desired/executable state.
25	3. Architecture and standards own durable boundaries and enforceable policy.
26	4. Dated proof/evidence owns one artifact/environment/authority observation and
27	   its limitations.
28	5. Active SPEC/tasks and execution plans own current implementation intent.
29	
30	Provider/registry output cannot grant authority. Completed plans are history.
31	Local release checks do not prove npm publication or external consumers.
32	
33	## Metadata and lifecycle
34	
35	New or materially revised maintainer docs separate `document_type`,
36	`lifecycle`, `authority`, and `owner`. Current durable docs also record
37	`last_reviewed` and `review_trigger`; superseded/tombstone docs record a
38	successor and reason.
39	
40	Lifecycle values are `proposed`, `current`, `implemented`, `superseded`,
41	`historical`, `evidence`, `reference`, `failed`, `inconclusive`, `tombstone`,
42	and `archived`. Authority values are `canonical`, `supporting`, `generated`,
43	and `external`. Legacy `status: canonical` is an authority marker, not a
44	lifecycle; migrate it only when its owner is materially revised.
45	
46	## Routes
47	
48	| Need | Owner | Use |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| Architecture | [`architecture/README.md`](architecture/README.md) | Current architecture route. `architecture.md` is a tombstone only. |
51	| Standards | [`standards/README.md`](standards/README.md) | Current durable engineering/documentation rules. |
52	| Current intent | [`product-specs/index.md`](product-specs/index.md) and [`exec-plans/active/README.md`](exec-plans/active/README.md) | Only genuinely active work; implemented/history stays inventory. |
53	| Completed history | [`exec-plans/completed/README.md`](exec-plans/completed/README.md) | Historical provenance, never default policy. |
54	| Public docs product | [`../apps/docs/README.md`](../apps/docs/README.md), [`../packages/docs-content/README.md`](../packages/docs-content/README.md), and [`../packages/docs-fumadocs/README.md`](../packages/docs-fumadocs/README.md) | Consumer-facing content/runtime, not maintainer lifecycle policy. |
55	| Repeatable release/deployment/recovery operations | [`runbooks/README.md`](runbooks/README.md) and [`operations/authority-model.md`](operations/authority-model.md) | Exactly five target-owned procedures; stop consequential operations when principal, candidate, target or receipt is unknown. |
56	| CI controls and recurring automation | [`standards/controls.md`](standards/controls.md) and [`operations/automation-register.md`](operations/automation-register.md) | Quality workflow admission, release-graph controls, and report-only candidate boundaries; neither route grants external authority. |
57	| Verification/critical journeys/proof | [`architecture/testing-and-quality.md`](architecture/testing-and-quality.md), [`verification/critical-journeys.json`](verification/critical-journeys.json), [`evidence/releases/HGI-203-critical-journeys.json`](evidence/releases/HGI-203-critical-journeys.json), [`evidence/releases/HGI-203-local.json`](evidence/releases/HGI-203-local.json), and [`documentation-audit/HGI-203-validation.json`](documentation-audit/HGI-203-validation.json) | The current inventory owns evolving journeys. Accepted HGI-203 retains the exact historical five-journey snapshot and bounded local proof that its immutable packet observed; HGI-204 validates both epochs without attributing current changes to the old attempt. Raw logs and secrets are never durable proof. |
58	| Harness foundation and requalification | [`verification/repository-harness-profile.json`](verification/repository-harness-profile.json), [`documentation-audit/harness-foundation/accepted-findings.json`](documentation-audit/harness-foundation/accepted-findings.json), [`verification/harness-epochs.md`](verification/harness-epochs.md), and [`verification/effectiveness.md`](verification/effectiveness.md) | The TaxKit profile, accepted HE crosswalk, content-addressed skill receipt and focused gate own the implemented baseline. Current epoch `HFI-004-2026-07-24` qualifies fail-closed candidate `7c8a96e`; HGI-206 remains previous history. Neither establishes external state. |
59	| References | [`references/README.md`](references/README.md) | Revalidate mutable external guidance. |
60	| Audit/accounting | [`documentation-audit/README.md`](documentation-audit/README.md) | Dated evidence, not policy. |
61	
62	Failed/inconclusive work retains provenance, last successful step, observed
63	state, escalation, resume trigger, recovery, and non-claims outside default
64	current routes. Do not delete or move historical/public/binary evidence without
65	an approved retention manifest.
66	
67	## Maintenance
68	
69	Every material slice decides `Change required`, `Preserve`, or `N/A` for docs,
70	READMEs, architecture, standards, public/generated references, runbooks,
71	proof/evidence, skills, lint/config/CI, and active SPEC/tasks. Update the
72	earliest durable owner and necessary pointers in the same slice. Counts prove
73	accounting only; semantic and consumer claims need owner review and
74	boundary-matched proof.
75	
76	Use the repository-local `$docs-maintainer` skill for this impact decision on
77	both PRD and ordinary changes. `$docs-writer` is limited to public-copy wording
78	after the maintenance route has selected the owner; it cannot close lifecycle,
79	generated-content, package, proof, or validation work. Background freshness
80	scans produce report-only candidates and cannot publish policy or documentation
81	without separately attached implementation authority, review and publication
82	identity.
83	
84	`bun run check:docs` enforces the mechanical owner contract in
85	[`../tools/documentation/owner-policy.json`](../tools/documentation/owner-policy.json).
86	It checks maintainer metadata, links, documented commands, workspace README
87	coverage, public/maintainer separation, accepted public-status representation,
88	and generated-source edges with bounded diagnostics and a JSON detail receipt.
89	`draft` means authored, locally renderable, visibly labelled candidate content;
90	`published` means explicitly accepted current public documentation. Neither
91	status proves runtime or external availability.
92	
93	`bun run check:runbooks` Schema-decodes the canonical runbook contract, the
94	current journey inventory and the exact historical HGI-203 journey snapshot,
95	then reconciles the immutable packet digest, four Markdown owners, commands,
96	evidence paths, stop operations, index rows and authority rows. It writes only
97	the ignored bounded receipt `tmp/runbook-validation-report.json`, executes none
98	of the documented procedures and establishes no consequential state.
